questions.question: Why does the KV cache create a memory problem during long-text generation?
options: Because it stores only the final output
Because it stores Key and Value information for many past words in memory
Because it removes positional information
Because it replaces attention with convolution

questions.question: Why could earlier AI models usually handle only shorter inputs?
options: They did not use any data
The memory needed for stored context became too large for long texts
They could not generate tokens
They were trained only on images

questions.question: What is the main goal of context engineering?
options: To make every model smaller
To help models process very long documents efficiently
To eliminate the need for GPUs
To remove the KV cache completely

questions.question: Sparse Attention works by:
options: Comparing every word with every other word
Focusing only on nearby and some important distant words
Ignoring all distant context entirely
Rotating the word embeddings

questions.question: What is the main trade-off of Sparse Attention?
options: It increases memory usage but improves full context understanding
It saves memory but slightly reduces full context understanding
It removes the need for training data
It prevents long-text generation

questions.question: Ring Attention is most useful because it:
options: Processes long text across multiple GPUs by dividing the work
Stores all words in a single hidden layer
Uses fixed positions instead of relative positions
Only works on short prompts

questions.question: In Ring Attention, large text is first:
options: Converted into images
Divided into parts and processed across multiple GPUs
Compressed into one token
Turned into labels

questions.question: How does Ring Attention help with very long inputs?
options: By forcing the model to ignore most words
By allowing systems to share information while processing different parts
By removing the need for memory
By using only one GPU for everything

questions.question: RoPE stands for:
options: Rotary Position Embedding
Relative Output Position Encoding
Recurrent Position Evaluation
Randomized Prompt Embedding

questions.question: What is the main idea behind RoPE?
options: Assigning fixed positions to words permanently
Rotating the mathematical representation of words based on position
Deleting all positional information
Using only absolute distances between tokens

questions.question: Why is RoPE useful for long sequences?
options: It helps the AI understand how far apart words are
It reduces the number of training examples needed to zero
It eliminates the need for tokenization
It prevents the use of attention

questions.question: Compared to fixed positional encoding, RoPE emphasizes:
options: Relative positioning
Image resolution
Training data cleaning
Token cost reduction only

questions.question: Which three factors are highlighted by scaling laws?
options: Model size, training data, and computing power
Token count, punctuation, and file type
Memory, latency, and accuracy
Queries, keys, and values

questions.question: What is the key idea of scaling laws?
options: Only model size matters
Performance depends on balancing model size, data, and compute
More layers always solve every problem
Training data is optional if the model is large enough

questions.question: Why is increasing only model size not enough according to scaling laws?
options: Because the model also needs enough training data
Because larger models cannot use attention
Because larger models only work on short texts
Because compute becomes irrelevant

questions.question: Scaling laws help engineers mainly by:
options: Designing smarter and more cost-effective AI systems
Removing the need for GPUs
Replacing tokenization with raw text
Making all models identical

questions.question: Which technique is most directly aimed at reducing memory pressure by selective focus?
options: Sparse Attention
Ring Attention
RoPE
Scaling Laws

questions.question: Which technique is most directly aimed at distributing long-text work across multiple GPUs?
options: Sparse Attention
Ring Attention
RoPE
KV Cache

questions.question: Which technique is most directly related to improving positional understanding in long sequences?
options: RoPE
Sparse Attention
Ring Attention
KV Cache

questions.question: Which option correctly matches the technique to its main role?
options: KV Cache — rotates word positions
Sparse Attention — compares every word with all others
Ring Attention — splits text across GPUs for long inputs
Scaling Laws — stores keys and values in memory
